## 1) Run AUB autopilot (module-level search + pick best)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
**Purpose:** Sweeps module candidates listed in the registry, runs evals, and if a candidate beats the current champion on the configured criteria, it will mark/select it as best.

**Check after it finishes:**
- A new “best”/selected candidate was produced (or explicit message that none beat the champion).
- Any failures/timeouts: note which module/candidate and why (dependency, config, runtime).

**Artifacts to preserve for handoff:**
- The console log (or run log file if the tool writes one).
- Any updated “champion” file if it auto-promotes.

## 2) Run system autopilot (system-level candidate sweep)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
**Purpose:** Tests full-system candidate configurations defined in `system_candidates.yaml` (end-to-end, not just individual modules).

**Check after it finishes:**
- Any candidate surpasses champion on your key metrics (you listed `tuning_mean/min` and `lockbox_mean/min`).
- Whether improvements are robust (e.g., not only improving mean while tanking min, unless your selection logic allows that).

**Artifacts to preserve:**
- Summary table/report of candidates and scores.
- Any generated config snapshots for top candidates.

## 3) Generate the “next fix” plan (actionable todo list)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
**Purpose:** Produces a markdown plan of the most promising fixes/next changes based on current results and registry state.

**Check after it finishes:**
- `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` exists and is readable.
- It references the latest runs (not stale run IDs).

  1) find a new PASS via step (1) or (2), or  
  2) produce a clear prioritized fix plan via step (3) if everything fails.

If you paste the stdout summaries (or the resulting report tables) after running (1) and (2), I can help interpret whether anything truly beats the champion given your mean/min tradeoffs.
